71-015.r: Lahore Session (December 1929, President Jawaharlal Nehru) → Purna Swaraj adopted as goal; Moderate-Extremist rift ended at Lucknow 1916, not Lahore; no resolution against two-nation theory.

71-021.r: Lahore resolutions (31 December 1929): Round Table Conference useless, Dominion Status dropped, Swaraj = Complete Independence, Civil Disobedience authorised; abolition of untouchability not included.

71-022.r: Madras Session 1927 → President Dr. M.A. Ansari; rejected Simon Commission; objected to Indian troops in China; Purna Swaraj not adopted there → (ii) and (iii) not true.

71-023.r: Poorna Swaraj Resolution at Lahore → moved by J.L. Nehru ('we have but one goal today, that of independence'); Nehru Report's Dominion Status rejected.

72-001.r: Lahore Session (1929) authorised Congress Working Committee to launch Civil Disobedience; Gandhi named leader at CWC meeting, Sabarmati Ashram, February 1930.

72-002.r: Dandi March (12 March 1930, Sabarmati to Dandi, 241 miles, 24 days) → began Civil Disobedience; reached Dandi 5 April, broke salt law 6 April 1930.

72-008.r: Civil Disobedience (1930) began from Dandi, by breaking the salt law; BPSC key said Sabarmati, which the book calls incorrect.

72-009.r: Dandi March: most Satyagrahis from Gujarat (32), then Maharashtra (13), U.P. (8).

72-010.r: Salt Satyagraha aimed to break salt law (Salt Act 1882), curtail government power and press for repeal of salt laws → more than one option; Purna Swaraj not its aim.

72-011.r: Salt Satyagraha participants → Sarojini Naidu, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, Kamladevi Chattopadhyaya (all of these); women played a leading part.

72-012.r: Maximum women's participation → Salt Satyagraha (Civil Disobedience): picketing liquor and foreign cloth shops; Sarojini Naidu led raid on Dharsana Saltworks.

72-013.r: Civil Disobedience 1930 → started from Dandi (Navsari, Gujarat), salt law broken 6 April 1930; march from Sabarmati on 12 March with 80 volunteers, 241 miles, 24 days.

72-018.r: First event → Simon Commission's arrival (3 February 1928); then Dandi March (12 March 1930), Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931), Quit India (9 August 1942).

72-019.r: 6 April 1930 → Gandhi broke salt law at Dandi, starting Civil Disobedience; Subhas Bose likened it to Napoleon's march from Elba to Paris.

72-020.r: Salt agitation launched 1930 (A true); aim was not free salt for poor (R false) → Gandhi's 11 demands to Irwin included abolishing salt tax and government salt monopoly.

72-021.r: Gandhi was arrested after breaking salt law (1 false); Madan Mohan Malviya, Devadas Gandhi, K.M. Munshi, B.G. Kher, Mahadev Desai, Rajagopalachari convicted for it (2 true).

72-022.r: 'I want world sympathy in this battle of Right against Might' → Gandhi to journalists at Dandi (5 April 1930), Dandi March.

72-023.r: 'Sedition has become my religion (Dharma)' → Gandhi, Salt Satyagraha-Dandi March speech, 18 March 1930.

72-024.r: Dandi March: from Sabarmati Ashram (12 March 1930, not 15 March), 241 miles on foot, ended at seaside Dandi; book marks 'Gandhi prepared salt at seashore' as incorrect.
72-024.c: Key (c) is debatable: at Dandi Gandhi picked up a lump of salty mud and, by many accounts, boiled it in seawater to make salt, so (c) can be read as true.

72-026.r: After Gandhi's arrest in Salt Satyagraha → Abbas Taiyabji led the movement.

72-027.r: Gandhi arrested 5 May 1930 → in Yerwada Jail during Dharsana Salt Depot raid; Abbas Taiyabji then arrested; Sarojini Naidu led raid on 21 May 1930.

72-028.r: Vinoba Bhave first arrested in 1930 → for taking part in Civil Disobedience Movement.

72-029.r: Webb Miller, American journalist, stayed with Gandhi at Sabarmati Ashram during Dandi March; reported police brutality at Dharsana.

72-030.r: Foreign journalist who reported Dharsana salt works Satyagraha → Webb Miller (American); marchers were beaten but did not resist.

72-032.r: Vedaranyam March (Tanjore coast, April 1930) to break Salt Law → C. Rajagopalachari; second such march after Dandi.

72-033.r: Khudai Khidmatgars ('Red Shirts', 1929, NWFP) → Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan; Pathan regional nationalist unity and struggle against colonialism; active in Civil Disobedience.

72-037.r: Peshawar Incident (1930, Civil Disobedience) → Garhwal Rifles under Chandra Singh Garhwali refused to fire on unarmed crowd.

72-039.r: Jiatrang Movement → Manipur; led by Naga tribal woman Rani Gaidinliu during Civil Disobedience.

72-040.r: Agitation against Chaukidari Tax in Begusarai → part of Civil Disobedience Movement.

72-041.r: Salt Satyagraha at Bihpur, Bhagalpur → Mahadev Lal Sarraf (with Deep Narayan Singh, Rameshwar Narayan Agrawal and others).

72-042.r: Salt Satyagraha in Bihar → people also opposed the Chowkidari tax (paid for village watchmen); farmers refused it in 1930 → none of the options.

72-043.r: After Civil Disobedience failed → Gandhi stressed constructive programmes; founded All India Anti-Untouchability League (September 1932); retired from active politics 1934.

72-044.r: Dr. Radhabai arrested on 13 June 1932 while leading a procession in Second Civil Disobedience Movement.

72-045.r: Prabhavati Devi → freedom fighter from Patna; other Bihar women: Rajvanshi Devi, Suniti Devi, Radhika Devi.

73-001.r: Gandhi-Irwin Pact → 5 March 1931, before Second Round Table Conference; aim: ease Congress participation in RTC; Congress to stop Civil Disobedience.

73-003.r: Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931): Congress joins Second RTC; ordinances withdrawn; release only of prisoners not charged with violence; no inquiry into police excesses.

73-008.r: Gandhi-Irwin talks (mid-February 1931) arranged by Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jaykar; Gandhi freed 26 January 1931; pact signed 5 March 1931.

73-009.r: Mediators in Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jaykar; Sarojini Naidu called Gandhi and Irwin 'The Two Mahatmas'.

73-011.r: Alan Campbell Johnson (Irwin's biographer) called Gandhi's gains in Gandhi-Irwin Pact 'Consolation Prizes' (UPPSC revised key; first key said S.C. Bose).

74-001.r: Karachi Session (29-31 March 1931) → President Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; approved Gandhi-Irwin Pact; first resolutions on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme.

74-002.r: Karachi Session 1931 resolution on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme → drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru with M.N. Roy's help.

74-004.r: Subhas Chandra Bose called the Karachi Session (1931) the 'pinnacle of Mahatma Gandhi's popularity and prestige'.

74-005.r: Order (1931): Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March) → Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev hanged (23 March) → Karachi Session (March) → Second Round Table Conference.
74-005.h: P-E-K-R: Pact, Execution, Karachi, Round Table.

74-007.r: Order: Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) → Bhagat Singh executed (23 March 1931) → Karachi Session (from 29 March 1931) → Poona Pact (24 September 1932).

74-008.r: Order: Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) → Jallianwala Bagh (13 April 1919) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) → August Offer (1940).

75-001.r: First Round Table Conference (November 1930 to January 1931, London) → 89 Indian delegates incl. Maulana Mohammad Ali; Congress did not attend.

75-003.r: First RTC (St. James Palace, London, 1930-31; chaired by PM Ramsay MacDonald; Congress absent) → Indian Christians represented by K.T. Paul.

75-005.r: Second RTC (7 September to 1 December 1931) → Gandhi sole Congress representative; also Sarojini Naidu, Madan Mohan Malviya, Annie Besant; not Maulana Azad.

75-006.r: Second RTC (7 September to 1 December 1931): Gandhi (Congress), Sarojini Naidu, Annie Besant, Malaviya, Mahadev Desai, Ambedkar, Pyarelal; Jawaharlal Nehru and Rajendra Prasad absent.

75-010.r: Second RTC (1931) → Congress represented by Gandhi, not Jawaharlal Nehru (A false); Gandhi-Irwin Pact implied Congress participation (R true).

75-012.r: For Second RTC Gandhi sailed on S.S. Rajputana and stayed at Kingsley Hall, London.

75-014.r: Congress first took part in a Round Table Conference → Second RTC (Gandhi sole representative); he returned in December 1931 empty-handed.

75-015.r: Congress was represented only at Second RTC → by Gandhi, who returned from London in December 1931 empty-handed.

75-017.r: Second RTC failed over communal question → Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for depressed classes, refused by Gandhi; ended 1 December 1931.

75-018.r: Attended all three Round Table Conferences → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru.
75-018.c: Answer not printed (*); explanation names both Ambedkar and Sapru, two of the options.

75-022.r: 'First, Second, Third' RTC is a misnomer → one Conference held in three sessions (1930-32), to discuss Simon Commission Report.

75-023.r: Third Round Table Conference → 17 November to 24 December 1932.

75-024.r: Congress did not take part in First and Third RTCs, attended only Second → answer 'more than one'.

75-025.r: Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for depressed classes at First RTC; Poona Pact gave them representation in local bodies and civil services; Congress skipped Third RTC → all true.
